'''''Trachelium caeruleum''''', [[common name]] '''blue throatwort''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Campanulaceae]] [[native plant|native]] to the Mediterranean, where its native range includes [[Algeria]], [[Morocco]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], and [[Sicily]].<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 23 January 2018}}</ref> It has also become [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in a few areas, including [[New Zealand]], the [[Azores]], and parts of mainland Europe.<ref name=grin/>
 
Growing to {{convert|120|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} wide, it is a woody-based erect [[herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]], with oval leaves and dense cushions of violet-purple flowers in summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The [[Binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''caeruleum'' means "dark blue".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=L.|title=RHS Latin for Gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref>

In [[temperate climate]]s this plant is usually grown as a [[Hardiness (plants)|half-hardy]] [[Annual plant|annual]] for summer [[bedding (horticulture)|bedding]] schemes or planters. It has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Trachelium caeruleum'' | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/18280/Trachelium-caeruleum/Details|accessdate=13 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 102 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 23 December 2018}}</ref>  There are many [[cultivar]]s with a variety of flower colors, including white, red, pink, and dark purple.<ref>Liang, R. and B. K. Harbaugh. (2001). [http://horttech.ashspublications.org/content/11/2/316.full.pdf Evaluation of ''Trachelium'' cultivars as cut flowers.] ''HortTechnology'' 11(2), 316-18.</ref>
